text:
Maria P (PM): Quick sync — got late-stage asks from two large customers asking for sub-60ms tail latency for short-chat flows. They specifically called out competitor X's routing shortcut. Thinking we should consider a small roadmap tilt to prioritize a low-latency routing + lightweight quantized variant for these customers. Thoughts?
Samir (Eng): Do we have telemetry showing this is a broad need or just those two accounts?
Maria P (PM): Sales says it's emerging across three trial accounts. Not across the whole cohort but enough that Jamie thinks it's revenue-moving.
Jamie (Sales): Yep — these are on the edge of signing if we can prove consistent latency under load. They care more about perceived snappiness than model size.
Anya (Research): We have a ~12% quality delta when moving to the 8-bit quantized variant on their prompts. Need to validate acceptable degradation. Can run evals on their prompt set in 48h.
Leo (Infra): Routing shortcut idea sounds like: route short-context requests to a trimmed model instance with priority scheduling + aggressive batching thresholds disabled. Can prototype in a day but infra risk is cache fragmentation.
Samir (Eng): Also need fallback policy if trimmed variant drifts on hallucination. We should keep canary + automatic fallback to full model for safety.
Maria P (PM): Proposed scope for a minimal ship: 1) routing policy + config toggle per customer, 2) trimmed/quantized model build, 3) canary and fallback gating, 4) launch criteria: <60ms p95 for short requests under 95th percentile load and no >3% quality regression on customer eval set. Is that reasonable?
Samir (Eng): Reasonable but timeline? If infra prototype 1 day, model quant 2 days, gating + rollout 3 days — optimistic 1 week. Might need to deprioritize a planned non-critical experiment.
Leo (Infra): Also need a low-risk deploy plan: stage -> shadow -> canary (5%) -> ramp. ops-bot will enforce canary windows.
ops-bot: Reminder: canary windows require 48h monitoring and automated rollback on error-rate spike >1%.
Anya (Research): I can run prompt-set evals today and provide a pass/fail vs the 3% quality threshold. If we fail, we can explore small distillation to close gap.
Jamie (Sales): If we can commit to the launch criteria and 2-week pilot SLA, I can lock the deals. They want a signed addendum for the pilot SLA.
Maria P (PM): Decision check: do we tilt sprint next week to deliver the minimal ship? Vote: +1 to tilt, -1 to keep current plan.
Samir (Eng): +1 (we'll drop the non-critical perf experiment).
Leo (Infra): +1 (ops support).
Anya (Research): +1 (I'll own evals).
Jamie (Sales): +1.
Maria P (PM): OK consensus. Next steps: Samir to spin up prototype and sketch rollback playbook, Anya runs evals and shares metrics, Leo prepares canary gating in the console, Jamie preps pilot contract. I'll update the roadmap doc and notify engineering leadership.
Samir (Eng): I'll post the prototype link here when ready.
Anya (Research): Eval plan: run 2k samples from their prompt set, compute BLEU/EM/brand-specific heuristics, and surface examples >0.05 drop.
Maria P (PM): Launch criteria restated in-channel so we have a clear bar: p95 latency <60ms for short flows, overall quality regression <=3% on customer eval set, canary at 5% for 48h with no rollback triggers.
Jamie (Sales): Sounds good. I'll request an internal SLA doc from Legal for the pilot addendum.
Samir (Eng): Quick question: do we expose the routing toggle via Console per-customer or via API flag? Console toggle preferred for pilot.
Maria P (PM): Console toggle first, API flag later. Keep it simple.
Leo (Infra): Noted — adding per-customer config to rollout config.
Maria P (PM): Thanks team. I'll file a lightweight spec and link it here. If anyone has major blockers, shout now.
Samir (Eng): No blockers yet.
Anya (Research): I'll post results by EOD tomorrow.
Jamie (Sales): I'll aim to get the signed pilot by EOW.
ops-bot: Deploy window scheduled: canary start 1758893600.
Maria P (PM): Closing — thanks everyone. We move forward with tilt. :tada:
